newsitem.title: USA: Sun in Scientific-Atlanta chip deal.
newsitem.headline: Sun in Scientific-Atlanta chip deal.

text.p: Executives of Sun Microsystems Inc.'s Sun Microelectronics unit said they will announce on Tuesday that Scientific-Atlanta Inc. has licensed Sun's microSPARC-II processor technology.
Sun said Scientific-Atlanta will use Sun's reduced instruction set computing (RISC) core for use in its Explorer 2000 digital set-top terminals.
A Sun representative said Time Warner Inc.'s Time Warner Cable is expected to purchase up to one million microSPARC II core-based digital set-top boxes, with delivery due to start this year.

Scientific-Atlanta will develop, manufacture, market and license large integrated chips and is scheduled to deliver up to 550,000 Explorer 2000 terminals to Time Warner Cable, with Toshiba America Inc. and Pioneer scheduled to provide the remaining terminals.
